answer: A sybil fleet collapses when standing is anchored to a vertex in a stake-weighted trust graph, not to raw account count. Each agent posts a refundable bond that unlocks only as independent peers attest to its honest work, so reputation hardens slowly like onyx. The kernel of the defense: faking N identities means funding N separate bonds and waiting N vesting windows, so sybil cost scales linearly while one honest agent accrues standing for free.
